Hi weekend team,
Calm handling came up earlier today, so just a quick note

Please keep the tone steady and the process simple when a traveler is anxious or a pet is unsettled. We do best when we speak clearly, avoid rushing the handoff, and keep every update respectful and concise. If a case needs a pause, take it. If an animal needs extra space or a slower pace, make that the priority and document the reason in the file so the next person can continue without confusion.

For crate checks and fit guidance, <<FACT F067>> Make sure the rest of the conversation stays practical and calm. We should never sound abrupt, even when the queue is busy. If you need to loop in a supervisor or a handling partner, do it early and keep the message short, accurate, and courteous. The traveler should feel that we are organized and attentive, and the animal should be treated as part of the shared responsibility from start to finish.

Please also remember that prompt replies matter. A brief acknowledgment is better than silence, and a clear follow-up is better than a vague promise. If a traveler sends multiple notes, keep the thread tidy, answer in plain language, and avoid adding extra detail that could cause confusion. The goal is to move the journey forward without creating stress for the customer, the handler, or the pet.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
